name: A generic question protocol for LocalLLMStepByStep with Qwen3-4B: aspect-first and clause-first questioning against the current protocol
registered_by: protocol-agent (owner, 2026-10-02: keep LocalLLMStepByStep; bring Qwen3-4B up to high correctness through a comprehensive generic question protocol; plan adopted in the journal event 'Step-by-step question protocol plan adopted')
kind: evaluation-only, minimal (no training). Dev data only; no sealed suite is read.
question: Does a generic numbered-choice protocol (13 answer kinds, an aspects checklist verified by regex cues, slot questions for limits, options, two-sided comparisons, exclusions, groups and definitions, clause decomposition with clause roles, and a forced-contrast confirmation) raise the correct rate of Qwen3-4B Q4 as a LocalLLMStepByStep oracle over the current protocol without adding wrong answers?
model: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_K_M (~/models/local-judge/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf), one llama-server started by tools/local-llm/serve.mjs (optimised runtime: dedicated steps slot, prompt cache, prewarmed stable prefix), thinking off, greedy. Reference only: Qwen3.8-27B Q4 with the final method on the same rows, one pass.

methods.B: aspect-first: 13 kinds, Q2 aspects checklist verified by the cue table (two-signal rule), slot handlers, validator-driven re-asks, forced-contrast confirmation; the message is one unit
methods.C: clause-first: 13 kinds, deterministic sentence and clause decomposition with a clause-role question per extra clause, aspects from the cue table only, slot handlers, re-asks, forced-contrast confirmation
methods.B-cue: B without the Q2 checklist (aspects from cues only); run only if D clearly beats A
methods.B-yesno: B with the old yes/no confirmation instead of the forced contrast; run only if D clearly beats A

rows.a: known forms F2-F9 of eval/smoke-reasoning/bench/manifest.jsonl (dev), stageRows per family with seed 20261002, the 40 rows of the T10 measurement excluded
rows.b: the 10 held-out forms of tools/datasets/diversity/generality.mjs, instances 1..N
rows.c: the 5 compositions of the same generator, instances 1..N
rows.n: the 20 natural questions tools/eval/generality/natural-v1.jsonl (all in every stage)
rows.tuning: protocol bugs are fixed only on a fresh random development pool disjoint from the measured rows: level a rows from stageRows seed 777 outside the 10-per-family measured set, level b/c instances 11..15; never on measured rows

stages: stage 1: 3 rows per form (a: 24, b: 30, c: 15, n: 20 = 89 rows) for A, B, C, D; stage 2: 5 per form only for arms still undecided; stage 3: 10 per form only when the paired bootstrap still straddles 0.
metrics: Per level and method: correct / wrong / unknown / invalid+failed (scoring of the symbolic-vs-llm harness and the generality rescore, natural rows judged as in eval-generality-v1), questions per message, p50/p95 wall latency of the formalization, slot attribution of the first diverging step for every non-correct row. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples over rows, seed 1) of the correct-rate difference D-A pooled over the levels and per level.

stopping_rules.decisive: lower bound of the 95% interval of D-A > 0, point estimate >= 10 pp, and wrong(D) <= wrong(A) + 1 row: stop and adopt D
stopping_rules.futility: upper bound of the 95% interval < 5 pp: stop, keep A
stopping_rules.broken: more than 20% of a method's stage-1 rows failed (unreadable answers, transport): stop that method, fix on the tuning pool, restart small and record the stop

hypotheses.H1: D is correct on at least 10 pp more rows than A pooled over levels a, b, c and natural, with no more wrong rows (+1 tolerated).
hypotheses.H2: The gain comes mostly from levels b and c (forms A cannot express: limits, two-sided comparisons, suppositions, definitions).
hypotheses.H3: Questions per message stay at most 14 and the p50 latency below 1.5 s with Qwen3-4B on the optimised runtime.

deviations: Stage 1 was decisive for every new method (B, C, D, B-cue, B-yesno vs A); stages 2 and 3 were not run. B was adopted (most correct, fewest wrong).

After stage 1, class fit, the 'where' place rule, the unknown-name guard and the no-invalid-circuit fallback were added because the stage-1 natural rows were mostly invalid circuits; they were tuned on 24 fresh natural questions (Haiku subagent) and all 89 measured rows were rerun with B (final-B). The final natural numbers are on rows seen before the change.

Level b is not held out for this protocol: it was tuned on instances 11-15 of the same forms. Stage 1 and the first final runs also had three level-b phrasings as kind examples in the prompt (before-event, group-threshold, count-difference); found by tools/eval/generality/heldout-check.mjs, replaced by known-form phrasings, and final B (Qwen3-4B) and the Qwen3.8-27B reference were rerun with the clean prompt.
world-v1 was rebuilt by commonsense-agent during the day; natural rows of A (stage 1) and of final B may have used different builds.
non_claim: Small dev samples; the numbers describe these forms with Qwen3-4B, not generality in general. Level b/c forms were not shown to the CodingAgent guide; the step-by-step protocol is generic by construction but was designed knowing the inventory of constructs, which includes those forms.
